item.title: Hot Inflation Lifts Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: US Treasuries slumped after hotter-than-expected inflation prompted traders to add to wagers that Federal Reserve officials will raise interest rates later this month and next year. David Rosenberg, Founder of Rosenberg Research, and Jim Bianco, Founder of Bianco Research, react to September CPI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mauritius Extends Curfew for Second Night After Unrest
item.description: The government of Mauritius will impose a curfew for a second night across the island’s main population centers after the worst unrest since 1999.
item.dc:creator: Kamlesh Bhuckory

item.title: ASML Up on Supply Plans; BlackRock Reports Earnings | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- BlackRock (BLK) shares are responding to this morning's earnings. BlackRock reported assets under management that met the average analyst estimate and adjusted EPS and Sales beat estimates. - ASML (ASML) shares are rising this morning after the company said it's searching for ways to produce more chip-making machines over the next two years due to soaring artificial intelligence spending. ASML said its current supply plans mean it won’t be able to fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028, and it's investigating ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase previously communicated. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bank Stocks Brace for Higher Rates
item.description: RBC Capital Markets Large Cap US Bank Analyst Gerard Cassidy joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why Bank of America’s regulatory settlement wasn’t a complete surprise and how rising rates could affect bank margins. He also discusses AI investment, credit risks, and State Street’s selloff as investors reassess expectations across the banking sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Washington Lifts Sanctions on Venezuela’s Top Lawmaker
item.description: The US lifted sanctions on Venezuela’s top lawmaker in another sign of warming relations between Washington and Caracas following the capture of Nicolás Maduro earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago

item.title: UGG Lenders Pick Lazard for Talks Over Fiber Operator’s Debt
item.description: Creditors to Unsere Grüne Glasfaser have picked Lazard Inc to advise them in talks over the troubled fiber operator’s debt load.
item.dc:creator: Libby Cherry and Giulia Morpurgo

item.title: India Will Overhaul Examination System, Says Education Minister
item.description: As the Indian government addresses weaknesses exposed by exam leaks, education minister Pralhad Joshi says that they will revamp the examination system using technology. He spoke on a host of topics, as the minister of multiple portfolios, with Bloomberg's Yvonne Man. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zambia Says Some Copper Sales to China to Be Settled in Renminbi
item.description: Zambia said Chinese buyers of its copper exports will start paying for some of their metal purchases in renminbi from next year, part of a growing move among African nations to use the Chinese currency instead of the dollar.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill

item.title: Phosphate Giant Seeks Foreign Investors as War Squeezes Finances
item.description: Morocco’s phosphate giant OCP SA is looking to attract foreign investors for some of its businesses, as supply disruptions caused by the Iran war hit profits at the state-owned company.
item.dc:creator: Souhail Karam

item.title: Anthropic Investor Day Focuses on Growth
item.description: Anthropic is holding an investor day as it advances plans for a potential IPO at an approximately $2 trillion valuation, amid growing concerns about AI safety and threats. Momei Qu of PSP Growth says market sentiment around AI is shifting quickly as new information emerges. Qu expects discussions to center on the trade-offs between growth and capital expenditures, as well as Anthropic’s anticipated valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CPI ‘Opens the Door More’ to October Fed Hike, Says PGIM’s Sockin
item.description: Robert Sockin, chief US economist at PGIM, says the US economy needs two more rate hikes at a minimum and that “the broader direction is up” for interest rates even if the Federal Reserve does not move at this month’s meeting. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Weighs More Hikes on Inflation Concerns
item.description: Barclays senior US economist Pooja Sriram said higher interest rates are a blunt tool that tighten financial conditions and hit rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and autos first. While rising Treasury yields and the bond selloff have added restraint, she said it is unclear whether conditions are restrictive enough. With oil prices rising again, further pressure on housing and auto demand could create uneven economic damage without resolving inflation. Sriram said the Fed’s approach, reflected in September meeting minutes, is focused on managing the risk that strong demand, persistent inflation or adverse supply shocks push prices higher. The Fed appears prepared to raise rates further, though she said a hike as soon as October is unlikely. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Resilient Growth Cushions Tech Amid Rising Rates
item.description: Julia Hermann of New York Life Management tells Vonnie that the current macro and market backdrop remains favorable: economic growth is resilient, and although rates are rising, they have not yet climbed enough to threaten the growth outlook. Addressing concern that remarks from Broadcom and Intel CEOs could signal a tech selloff, she says investor focus has shifted. After years of watching for a lower limit on company investment, markets are increasingly concerned that spending—first among hyperscalers and now in chips—could become so high that it threatens free cash flow. The segment’s on-screen headlines note a worldwide memory-chip stock tumble and an ongoing chip selloff as major-bank earnings begin. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dollar Advances to Highest Since May 2025 on Fed Hike Views
item.description: The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as a hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova

item.title: Treasuries Slump as Hot Inflation Lifts Fed Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: US Treasuries slumped after hotter-than-expected inflation prompted traders to add to wagers that Federal Reserve officials will raise interest rates later this month and next year.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie

item.title: Fast-Money Quants Are at Odds With Fundamental Stock Investors
item.description: Money managers who focus on economic growth and the strength of earnings are showing growing doubts about the rally in US stocks.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: US Mortgage Rates Reach 7.5%; Home-Buying Slump Hits Sixth Week
item.description: US mortgage rates continue to rise, pushing down home purchasing activity for a sixth straight week.
item.dc:creator: Michael Sasso

item.title: Gold Slumps as Faster US Inflation Stokes Fed Rate Hike Wagers
item.description: Gold slumped after US consumer prices jumped the most in five months, reigniting worries that the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates further to combat inflation.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan and Mark Burton

item.title: Allan Gray Sees Nigeria Rally Broader Than Korea’s AI Boom
item.description: Allan Gray Ltd., which oversees $29 billion in assets, sees Nigeria’s stock rally as more broad-based than South Korea’s, offering investors a diversification play from the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has swept markets from Wall Street to Asia.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks joined bonds lower as the fastest increase in inflation since April bolstered bets the Federal Reserve will keep lifting interest rates amid elevated energy costs.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth
